entities.title: Whether and how to publish MEG
entities.summary: MEG is published on icelander.net behind the sign-in, with a shared high-score table.
entities.context: Every other game is deployed by the workflow behind icelander.net's sign-in, and most have a replay-checked high-score table. MEG's simulation uses Math.random and Math.sin, so a replay-checked table would first need a deterministic engine with a seeded generator, as AGENTS.md requires.

options.title: Keep it as a static page in the repository
options.consequences: Nothing more to do; it is played by opening index.html.

options.title: Publish it on icelander.net behind the sign-in, without scores
options.consequences: Needs an npm project and a Worker that serves the page; the game itself is unchanged.

options.title: Publish it with a replay-checked high-score table
options.consequences: Also needs the engine split out and made deterministic, a score definition, and a D1 database with a migration.

entities.decision: Publish it on icelander.net behind the sign-in, with a shared high-score table of trusted scores (trusted-scores).
entities.rationale: The owner asked for the game to be published, and then for a high-score list.

entities.title: Trust MEG's scores from the browser, within checked limits
entities.summary: MEG's shared table takes the score the game sends; the server checks it is plausible but cannot replay the run.
entities.context: AGENTS.md says the server replays every submitted game. MEG's simulation uses Math.random, trigonometry and Math.hypot throughout, so it cannot be replayed exactly without rewriting its physics and AI.

options.title: Trusted scores
options.consequences: Hours of work. A ticket per run, used once, and a score the run's time could have earned; a determined cheater can still fake a plausible score.

options.title: Replay-checked
options.consequences: Cheat-proof like the other games, but a large rewrite of the simulation that could change how the game feels.

entities.decision: Trusted scores, as an exception to the replay rule for this game only.
entities.rationale: The owner chose it when asking for a high-score list.

entities.title: Keep MEG's table in a Durable Object, not a D1 database
entities.summary: The table lives in one SQLite-backed Durable Object, which a deploy creates, instead of a D1 database like the other games'.
entities.context: A new D1 database has to be created and migrated by hand in Cloudflare before the deploy (docs/database-migrations.md), and the session that built the table had no Cloudflare credentials. A Durable Object class is created by the migration in wrangler.jsonc when the Worker deploys.

options.title: Durable Object
options.consequences: Deploys with no hand step; one object holds the whole table, which is ample for a hundred rows.

options.title: D1 database
options.consequences: Matches the other games; needs the database created and its schema applied by someone with Cloudflare access first.

entities.rationale: It needs no step outside the deploy, and the table is small.
